after: ## What each unit measures in Topic 8
alt: Seven unit cards: kilogram (kg) for mass; metre (m) for distance and orbital radius; metre/second (m/s) for speed and velocity; metre/second² (m/s²) for acceleration; newton (N) for force including weight; second (s) for time and orbital period; newton/kilogram (N/kg) for gravitational field strength g.
caption: Each unit belongs to one quantity; learn the pairs.

after: ## Mass, weight and gravitational field strength
alt: A 75 kg astronaut has a weight of 75 × 10 = 750 N on Earth and 75 × 1.6 = 120 N on the Moon, with weight arrows drawn to the same scale; the mass is 75 kg in both places. W = m × g, so N = kg × N/kg, and N/kg is equivalent to m/s².
caption: Mass in kg is unchanged; weight in N depends on g.

alt: Conversion arrows: 1 km × 1000 = 1000 m; 1 h × 3600 = 3600 s; 1 day × 24 × 3600 = 86 400 s; 1 year × 365 × 86 400 ≈ 3.15 × 10⁷ s. Converting before substituting into v = 2πr / T gives m/s; otherwise the answer comes out in km/h.
caption: Kilometres to metres and hours, days or years to seconds, before substituting.

alt: A satellite orbits a planet. The orbital radius r runs from the centre of the planet to the satellite, so it equals the planet's radius plus the satellite's height above the surface.
caption: Orbital radius = planet radius + height above the surface.

after: ## Checking an answer with its units
alt: Unit checks: in v = 2πr / T, m ÷ s gives m/s; in W = m × g, kg × N/kg gives N; in T = 2πr / v, m ÷ m/s gives s; in Δλ / λ₀ = v / c, both sides cancel to a pure number. An answer in km/h or m/day means a conversion was missed.
caption: Treat units like algebra: they should cancel to the unit asked for.

alt: Three worked examples. A satellite at 26 600 km = 2.66 × 10⁷ m with T = 12 × 3600 = 43 200 s has v = 3.9 × 10³ m/s. Earth at 1.5 × 10¹¹ m with T = 3.15 × 10⁷ s has v = 3.0 × 10⁴ m/s. The Moon at 3.8 × 10⁸ m moving at 1000 m/s has T = 2.4 × 10⁶ s, about 28 days.
caption: Write each conversion on its own line, then substitute.
